source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Ignoring the finding and proceeding with the full feeding without much regard for this result, contrary to what this elevated residual volume actually calls for","B":"Immediately double the feeding rate to compensate, similar to what the colleague is currently suggesting doing in response to this finding","C":"Automatically discontinuing essentially all future feedings permanently, which overstates the appropriate response to a single elevated residual reading","D":"Follow facility protocol for the residual volume threshold, rather than doubling the rate as the colleague suggested"}}
source_row.rationale: When an unusually high gastric residual volume is obtained, the nurse should follow facility-specific protocol (since exact threshold recommendations and practices continue to evolve and vary), which may include holding or delaying the feeding, reassessing the client, and notifying the provider if the finding persists or if the client shows other signs of feeding intolerance (such as nausea, vomiting, or abdominal distention), rather than an automatic, rigid response.
source_row.source_detail: Appropriate Response to Elevated Gastric Residual Volume
